I have mixed feelings about the current state of the game. I've played the earlier free demos, and the game has changed a bit from those days. On the plus side: Updated gameplay with gameplay difficulty modes, and instead of collecting static weapons in C-B-A categories, you can merge weapons (and parts) to improve them to A or S rank, which is interesting. On the minus side: The cargo mechanic was poorly implemented. Seems straightforward at first. Collect cargo packages and deliver them to hazard research sites for small rewards. But the game isn't super clear about the fact that the 'cargo' slot you equip isn't cargo. It's a frame that lets you pick up small cargo boxes in the map, or load up cargo boxes that were collected by the scrapper. The thing I don't like about the cargo mechanic is that it's directly tied to the map biome switching EVERY TIME you beat a boss or visit the scrapper. There was one biome map with a TON of cargo boxes. But there was a catch. The boxes were scattered across a mountain range, and the three research sites WERE ALL AT THE PEAKS OF THE MOUNTAIN RANGE. This meant that I had to sloooooowly drive up the mountain range, inch by inch, risking the possibility of LOSING THE CARGO BECAUSE THE CARGO PARTS RANK WASN'T HIGH ENOUGH, being ambushed by enemy cars that wanted the cargo, and so on and so forth. There was one point where I took a moment to sit still and find the best way to climb the last part of the mountain range, and then, VINES SPROUTED FROM THE GROUND AND TOOK AWAY ALMOST HALF OF MY CAR'S HEALTH BAR BEFORE I DROVE DOWN THE MOUNTAIN RANGE IN A PANIC. At no point was this foreshadowed by the gameplay or story. Kaizo traps are not an improvement over micro-transactions. I had already learned that visiting the scrapper changes the biome, thus making all of the cargo boxes on the map disappear, so I kept struggling and struggling and struggling until I decided it wasn't worth the hassle. I gave up, visited the scrapper to upgrade my cargo slot to S, and then, the biome changed like I knew it would. I can't recommend the game in this state as the cargo mechanic isn't properly tuned and balanced in implementation, AND THE DEVELOPER IS APPARENTLY A SADIST WHO EQUATES FRUSTRATION = HARDER = BETTER.
Making a long forgotten thing about gaming: >No micro-transactions >No paid DLCs >Community shared skins >You play the game to earn stuff >No currencies >No gacha

I normally write reviews in the 100 hour rule - if you haven't played the game for 100 hours then you don't know the game. However, in this specific case, I know this game after just 1 hour. It's a unity game (no issues there) that is priced far above its content. Loop is go shoot stuff, get better stuff for your car, progress. Not a bad idea, except: Your "base" is 6? tabs that allow you to rearm, replace or rebuild your car. Your "world" outside that is go shoot things - the default controls are bad (no, I do not want to reach across my keyboard to "honk twice" to get my base to stop so I can drive into it when I have to take my hand off my mouse to do so). Neither do I want the controls to be so over-twitchy that I may as well not drive anything but by holding down the W key, in case I just randomly do a 360 degree spin. Nor do I want my weapon choices to be dictated as the base weapons in the game, due to the fact I can upgrade them via merging other same looted weapons so much that any other choices are completely redundant, until I can max the next options to the same level. This is a good concept, really badly implemented. It pains me to say that, as I really support indie dev teams coming up with new concepts, as I believe that they are the ones that drive the gaming industry on, not triple A houses. For that reason alone, I have not requested a refund for this game. If you want the same genre and price, there are better titles. I won't mess over the dev team by mentioning them here. Sorry for this review - if you reworked it from the ground up, I think you may well have something good, but at the price point you are asking and the content you are providing, it's a solid no from me.

This is a hard one. I've been playing Fumes since the demo released. I've seen numerous iterations of the game and how much work the Devs have put into it...but I can't recommend the game as it is right now. I'll cute to the chase, everything is great, but the endgame is grindy and boring. Introducing weapon grades and upgrades was a fantastic move, but the drop rates are awful. If you want 2-3 maxed out S Rank weapons, prepare to spend hours a day for a week or more. And even then you're wasting your time if you're not grinding rocket launchers. I remember the Autocannon and Pounder weapons being S Tier weapons and now they kinda suck? Everything else is fantastic and I love Fumes to death, but for the love of God let us turn unwanted weapons into scrap so I can upgrade something I want. Buff the Autocannon and Pounder. The Devs truly have something special here, but the endgame just makes me want to uninstall it.

While it pains me to say so, as I see great potential in FUMES, I could not with clear conscience recommend this product thus far, and I am a little surprised by the overwhelmingly positive review consensus so far. Having completed the game in its current state, here's a few thoughts. Firstly, allow me to make it clear that my thoughts are mostly around what FUMES does [i]not[/i] have or do at this moment, rather than what has already been built. In other words, there remains great potential, and I am confident that the game as a whole will continue to be refined and expanded. However, in its current form, it is much closer to a [b]tech demo[/b] rather than a complete, gaming product. To start with some positives, FUMES looks and feels great. There is a coherent visual art style present all throughout that required not a trivial amount of planning and dedicated craft, and it sets the game apart. A lot of attention has been given to the core mechanics so far - the driving, shooting, UI - and it gives the game the feeling of being a lot closer to completion than the rest of the content. But speaking of the content - it is almost laughably absent. In its current state FUMES offers little worthwhile fun... at all. There is a grand total of about 3 mission types (with some variety in flavor, but at the center still within the same constraints) - destruction, escort and race. That's really about it - and it's even a lot more monotonous than the previous sentence would make you feel. To complete the game, each mission type is replayed over and over and over again - each mission no less than 10 or more times. Even [i]within[/i] those missions variety is lacking; each mission consists of waves of brainless enemies hurling at you in waves, on repeat, over and over again. Race being one exclusion, but in itself it's a weird beast - race courses are designed in an incredibly confusing pattern, I assume by someone who has seen circuit racing through a 12-inch TV screen from a bus riding at top speed, for no other explanation could breathe clarity into why each lap of every course looks like a dash from A to B through more-or-less straight path with checkpoints, only then to bring you all the way back from B to A [i]without checkpoints[/i] to start a new lap. Incredible. Difficulty is generally abysmal. Currently FUMES is not a challenge in any way, shape or form. Enemies appear to try some specific strategies based on their equipment but it hardly matters, because generally all throughout the game each 'regular' enemy is as much of a danger as a fly landing on your leg during a summertime campfire. Enemies seem to be nearly completely incapable of substantially damaging you, as you can tank thousands of shots with no issue whatsoever, while they themselves die from a few well-placed shots. Later on in the game, once equipped with three rocket launchers, you are easily able to clear any regular opponent in one shot. So the game turns to clearing exhaustively long waves of vehicle meat entirely harmless to yourself while doing the same mission type for the n-th time. Absolutely nothing of note happens during these missions and I only managed to fail a mission one time during the entire playthrough, as I was equipped with rocket launchers powerful enough to destroy the cargo truck I was escorting in effectively one shot. Oops. Beyond this FUMES can hardly be called a game due to a lack of any challenge or mission content whatsoever. One difficulty-related criticism is with the 'boat-like' boss enemies, who are generally likewise inept and of no concern to the player, except for one specific badly-coded attack. Their 'mortar' launches select a particular area of effect every now and then which is coded so that when driving at low speeds in low gear (which will happen eventually when circling a boss for the 126th time while dodging environmental obstacles) it can activate quite literally on top of you. I have tested that there are instances where this can happen without any possibility of recourse - it is physically impossible, even with the fastest car, to escape this radius at times before explosion, meaning that it effectively serves as an impossible to avoid punishment from gods. I have failed a boss fight twice because this happened to me five times in a row without any possibility of escaping. How fun. Despite my rambling FUMES clearly has a bright future - at the core, the game [i]can[/i] be fun, and there is doubtlessly tons of enjoyment in wheeling and shooting at stuff, especially in this enticing visual style and somewhat interesting level design. But FUMES as-is is little more than a tech demo with [i]some[/i] game features built on top of it, but hardly enough for maybe 30 minutes of genuine enjoyment, let alone a full playthrough. There is so, so much to be excited about here, and FUMES can be built into a fantastic game, with so many potential mission types, a much re-hauled combat system introducing some [i]actual[/i] challenge, refined game world and so much. But right now, it is not in any way worth the meager money spent on it beyond simply seeing what this tech demo offers before the full game is developed around it.

FUMES starts off strong but quickly turns stale. The big bosses are cool, but the mob fights are repetitive, and the only thing that changes from one mob fight to the next is the number of enemies. There are no new mechanics as the game progresses, and no interactions with the map aside from some destructible elements. With a barren map and a gameplay curve that adds nothing new, just more enemies in greater numbers, FUMES' gameplay quickly boils down to holding W while shooting cars around you until they're all destroyed. It's a shame because the weapons are cool and the driving feels nice, but how nice the driving is doesn’t matter, since the game never takes advantage of it. As it stands, I can't recommend FUMES. It fails to capture what made Vigilante 8, Twisted Metal, and Interstate '76 great. And if it's trying to be an arena shooter, where the main point is defeating lots of enemies, then the enemies simply don’t have enough variety to challenge the player. Play any of the new DOOM games and focus on the combat elements, on how enemies interact with the mechanics. Combat should essentially be a sort of puzzle. Now, for the obvious: I understand the game is in Early Access, but my criticism of the product I experienced stands. I’ll gladly change my review to "recommended" as soon as the game improves. I've been keeping an eye on FUMES ever since the earliest demos released, and I’m eager to see the game grow.

Hey, all the UE5 devs out there, start taking notes. This game doesn't have Lumen. It doesn't have Nanite. I don't need to use DLSS and frame generation to get acceptable performance on a decent rig. It runs at 160+ FPS with 200% scaling at 1440P with amazing visual clarity. I can actually see what I'm shooting at. There isn't smearing and ghosting everywhere from badly implemented TAA. And yet, despite the retro graphics style, I'm actually completely immersed and having FUN playing a game instead of continuously juggling graphics settings trying to find the right balance of performance and fidelity. I'm a simple man. Give me a game that's actually fun to play, give me an option to crank the fidelity to the moon (supersampling, downsampling, etc.) and I'm happy and writing a glowing review. It's that easy. GG FUMES team. A band of brothers who can read a damned room.

The Demo of this game gave me so much hope and I finally bit the bullet and bought the game and I'm not impressed. Conceptually it's great and I had a ton of fun playing the game until the second rig boss, Treadarius or whatever that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥'s name is. I'm a bit biased and hate changing my class for literally anything other than what I've already set the class to do, so the fact that I'm essentially forced to play a mini van to get the health to survive the onslaught of rockets, not to mention the boss HEALS all of his turrets if you manage to destroy them before he hits 50% of his HP. It may seem like I'm just whining but genuinely Treadarius is that bad I don't even wanna play the game anymore. Pros: Fun gameplay, good soundtrack, simplistic controls and high speed fun (there's more but it's late I want to go play something that's not going to annoy me.) Cons: High speed fun isn't very fun during boss fights. EVERY enemy constantly out performs your engine and stat power so severely in these random "boosts" of speed they get that they're CONSTANTLY flying by the player and ahead of you or they catch up within about 2 seconds flat and bosses are included in this, it feels like I'm playing Mad Max or even worse, GTA V and dealing with the cops that just randomly get a boost in horse power to their engine. Weapons are fun, but the spread is AWFUL on most of the basic and consistent forms of DPS. Overall the game is like a solid 7/10 but needs a bit of adjustment I think, if I could give this a neutral rating, I absolutely would. Now all this being said, don't let MY take on these "issues" dissuade you from trying this game, it is A LOT of fun, it just needs a bit more polish imo.

At the moment Fumes is dumb fun. It is a bit mad max, a bit twisted metal, and bit click the banana. You are in a barren wasteland. You drive cars. You put guns on cars. You shoot other cars with guns. you put more guns on more cars and shoot more cars. What the devs need to work out to have a top tier game is "why?". Why not just use the best damage guns all the time? Why not just pick the car body with the most weapons available? Why should i care about NPCs fighting each other? Why should i put 100hrs into this? The game is still early access so the devs can certainly work this all out. It needs more story. It needs checks and balances on the weapons and enemies. It honestly needs factions. helping out passing other cars that get ganged up on just makes everyone attack you it seems. Fumes is a neat framework of a game. The customization is good, the combat and driving feels so amazing and the layout of how to progress feels great. That said, I think this is a good FRAMEWORK of a game. Not a good game (yet). I plan to keep playing it because it is fun but it needs more. The content they have clearly focused on is boss fights and vehicles which is great. The environments are sorely lacking in interesting features and variety. That has always been an issue I have with "wasteland" themed games; the environment is boring. Its so boring. And even worse so when its procedurally generated. So much of this game is ranging from flat to only slightly not flat terrain and that is so beyond bland and boring. I've played for a little over 2 hours and outside of the cooler bosses, I feel like I've seen what there is to see in the game and that kinda sucks to think. What is here is cool. But its repetitive to say the least. If they can find it in them to expand on the terrain features or something, I think it would make this game a solid 9/10. At the moment I'd say the first hour is a 10, but hour 2 is a 6. Hour 3 is feeling like a 5. Overall, its not bad, but I dont think I would recommend it to a friend. YET.

So far, this game is so fun and what is already there, with what the devs have planned for the future, makes me feel really positive that i'm going to get a lot out of this game! Starting off, aesthetically, just very good. Really appealing visuals, obviously the charm of like all the processing effects and that is great, but man getting into a zone with a bunch of trees and the big brutalist buildings, with all these cool little cars driving around, just really rocks. I love the bosses and the car designs, and the customizability of them (also being like, digestible changes stat-wise is nice too.) Gameplay is really fun, it feels good to do the loop of drive around, start an event, blow up cars, go to the scrapper and upgrade or change your car, go back do a different event, it's just good stuff. I think more random events that pop up would be cool, and potentially more things that kind of fill up the space between events, as of right now if you're intentionally going to a specific thing on the compass, it can be a little bit of empty space inbetween, not a dealbreaker but it is noticeable! BUT like i said, that is something that i'm assuming will feel less of an issue when the devs implement all the stuff they've said they want to do! I just like collecting car parts and improving them and putting them on my cute little car i can design and shooting at a massive monster-car, that rocks and i cant wait to see where this goes because it's already great and so promising!!! Big recommend to anyone who likes arcadey-car stuff, Twisted Metal, and/or gear collecting!

I was SUPER excited when I saw this game, it looks really sick. And even if my review is mostly focusing on negatives, I feel like there's still a good base on which the game could be great. I'd play more if it weren't for the 2 hour refund window, as in general the game got really repetitive almost instantly and I'd like to see if it stopped being repetitive. But in the 2 hours I played if you did 1 mission you've done them all basically. Even bosses it doesn't matter, they all feel the same, every enemy feels the same too aside from how tanky they are. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Positives: - Love the attitude/style - The menus and HUD being "physical" is really charming and way too rare in games - The art is mostly nice and charming (minor nitpick about texel density when it comes to art) - Feels pretty satisfying driving around and shooting - Music and sound effects is all solid (the filter on the enemy chatter is kind of fatiguing on your ears though) - I like that you can switch between a bunch of filters and stuff ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Negatives: 1. Aside from being more consistent with hitting your shots with a mouse, there's like no skill expression? - It doesn't matter how you drive, going off jumps or anything does nothing gameplay-wise and you can't meaningfully manipulate enemies to crash into hazards much or something. (walls, explosives, fire, oil etc) - There's like no decision making required in neither movement nor combat. - You can't meaningfully dodge or outmaneuver enemies in any fun way, you just hold on to your gas and spray bullets until enemies die. - Even if the driving and shooting is pretty basic, at least there could be critical ways to deal damage, weak spots, hazards you can use against them, ram them off cliffs etc would all at least give me something to do aside from "hold button 1 and button 2 until enemies dead". - There's also no enemy reactions. Like in an fps game dealing a certain amount of damage in a short enough time span might stagger an enemy, which in turn might affect their behavior. Here they just take it going from 100 to 0. - The terrain in the 2 hours I played was also mostly just flat ground, the few objects scattered around mostly didn't matter to gameplay. At most they'd obstruct some bullets flying around for a sec. --- 2. Extremely repetitive enemy/boss encounters, after you've done one you've done them all. --- 3. The UI is extremely unnecessarily clunky, so many clicks and button presses that could be mitigated. It's also not clear what each button press is about to do really. Like yea you can figure it out but for how simple the functions are it's oddly hidden in multiple menus when it feels like it could be streamlined. It's not like most of those things seemed to matter much anyway. The menu is borderline unusable with a controller so switched to kb+m - Why even have to go to the big mechanic truck to upgrade guns you're already using? Finishing enemy encounters doesn't give you anything exciting and all you really get is more of guns you already have, and you can then drive off to a truck and "merge" those guns onto your identical ones, which is just sort of boring incremental stat boosts like "+0.3 damage". Those types of stat boosts are never fun imo but even then it should not be a button you have to DRIVE to just to apply it. There's seemingly no reason I wouldn't want to apply it so.. just apply it... ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
